Commentary.Commentary: We are back. A mammoth task awaits for Pakistan and a lot rests on their top order. The players are out in the middle. Shaheen Afridi ended with five wickets, can the other left-armer, Starc replicate something similar....
... THE CHASE..

Pakistan on the other hand, will be very pleased with how they have come back into the game! They were battered at the start. Their pacers went the journey, they were dropping catches and their body language was quite poor. The spinners though, the likes of Mohammad Nawaz and Iftikhar Ahmed bowled quite tightly in the middle overs. Usama Mir was also decent but it was the death bowling which was brilliant. The likes of Shaheen Afridi, who was the pick and Rauf were excellent. Shaheen Afridi ended with a fifer and Rauf who went for around 60 in his first four, ended with three. Pakistan though still have a big target ahead of them and the wicket does not seem that easy. It oculd get better under lights but they will have to bat really well. Australia on the other hand, will believe they can defend this. An interesting second half awaits.

That is a serious comeback by Pakistan and they have momentum on their side heading into the break! At one stage, Australia looked all set for 400. Their openers got them off to an absolute flier. The two added over 200 and when they were batting, it was all carnage. Both scored tons. Marsh fell but Warner continued. However, after Marsh he kept losing partners at the other end. Warner though got his 150 up but once he fell, runs were not easy to come by. Australia only managed to score around 65 in the last 10 and they will be pretty disappointed with that.

The Australians usually come to life when it matters and we expect nothing different from them here.

It is the Aussies taking on Pakistan and it is being played in Bengaluru. It is the first game at this venue and we expect it to be an absolute cracker. A World Cup in any sport is incomplete without upsets, and the 2023 ODI World Cup is no different, with England and South Africa suffering shock defeats at the hands of Afghanistan and the Netherlands, respectively. These upsets make the competition even fiercer, and the stakes in big games become even higher. It is time for another big game in this World Cup as Australia take on Pakistan at the M Chinnaswamy Stadium in Bengaluru. A potential mouth-watering clash between two quality sides will mark the arrival of cricket's biggest carnival in India's Garden City, Bengaluru. The five-time champions, Australia, were off to the worst possible start with back-to-back losses but bounced back in the third game against Sri Lanka to collect their first points of the competition. A fighting display in the second half of their bowling effort helped them bowl out Sri Lanka for a modest total. In their pursuit of 210, the fifties from Mitchell Marsh and Josh Inglis, along with contributions from the rest of the middle order, sealed the deal for them. Australia had failed to breach the 200-run mark on consecutive occasions, and no batter had managed to score a fifty until the game against Sri Lanka. Having managed to cross both hurdles, Australia's batting unit will be confident ahead of the clash against Pakistan. However, their batting mainstays, David Warner and Steven Smith, have not had the impact they would have liked and will be eager to contribute to the team's cause with a big score. Mitchell Marsh returned to form with a fifty, as did Josh Inglis, justifying his selection in the team ahead of Alex Carey. Out of the many positives from that 5-wicket win, Adam Zampa's four-wicket haul will be the biggest of them all. In the post-match interview, Zampa said that he was suffering from back spasms before and during the game, and the Aussie fans will hope that the back holds up alright for their premier spinner. On the other hand, Pakistan's World Cup campaign hit a roadblock after suffering a crushing defeat to arch-rivals India in Ahmedabad. With two out of two wins, Pakistan were high on confidence, but a collapse of epic proportions with the bat meant that the elusive wait for the first win against India in ODI World Cups continued. It will not be easy for Babar Azam and Co. to put that loss behind them, and to add to their misery, illness has hit the Pakistan camp. What will come as a relief for Pakistan fans, though, is that two of their flu-affected players, Abdullah Shafique and Shaheen Afridi, returned to the training session that took place two days before the game. The silver lining for Pakistan against India was that Babar Azam's low run of ODI scores finally came to an end, and he will be keen to build on his form in the games to follow. With the ball, their new-ball attack of Shaheen Afridi and Hasan Ali lacked the cutting edge, as did Haris Rauf. In the spin department, Shadab Khan continued to prove expensive, while Mohammad Nawaz was slightly economical compared to his compatriot. If Pakistan are to pose a tough challenge to other teams, their bowlers will have to take their game up a notch. Out of the ten ODI World Cup meetings between these two sides, Australia have emerged victorious on six occasions. Will they extend their dominance? Or will Pakistan pull one back? We will find out soon enough.
